review_locator: PMCID:PMC6005205, Emerging roles of Atypical Chemokine Receptor 3 (ACKR3/CXCR7) in normal development and physiology; PMCID:PMC6052832, The unique structural and functional features of CXCL12
primary_title: Mutational Analysis of Atypical Chemokine Receptor 3 (ACKR3/CXCR7) Interaction with Its Chemokine Ligands CXCL11 and CXCL12
decision_basis: The reviews identify ACKR3/CXCR7 as a CXCL12-binding atypical receptor, and the cited primary mutational study maps CXCL12 binding, beta-arrestin recruitment, and chemokine degradation/scavenging at ACKR3.
limitations_preserved: Atypical receptor with scavenging and beta-arrestin responses rather than a classical G-alpha-i chemotaxis claim; preserve CXCL12 monomer/dimer and CXCR4 context.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6005205, Emerging roles of Atypical Chemokine Receptor 3 (ACKR3/CXCR7) in normal development and physiology; PMCID:PMC6052832, The unique structural and functional features of CXCL12
primary_title: Proteolytic processing of CXCL11 by CD13/aminopeptidase N impairs CXCR3 and CXCR7 binding and signaling and reduces lymphocyte and endothelial cell migration; Mutational Analysis of ACKR3/CXCR7 Interaction with CXCL11 and CXCL12
decision_basis: The reviews identify CXCL11 as an ACKR3/CXCR7 ligand, and the cited primary studies support CXCL11 binding/signaling, receptor-interface dependence, beta-arrestin recruitment, and scavenging; proteolytic processing changes the interaction.
limitations_preserved: Proteolytic processing affects binding and signaling; ACKR3 is atypical/biased rather than a universal classical G-protein receptor, and CXCR3 remains a separate canonical receptor.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC4901034, Atypical Chemokine Receptors and Their Roles in the Resolution of the Inflammatory Response; PMCID:PMC6176735, Chemokine Transport Dynamics in Lymphatic and Blood Vessels
primary_title: ACKR4 on Stromal Cells Scavenges CCL19 To Enable CCR7-Dependent Trafficking of APCs from Inflamed Skin to Lymph Nodes
decision_basis: The reviews identify ACKR4 as a scavenger for CCL19/CCL21, and the cited primary study shows ACKR4-dependent CCL19 scavenging by mouse skin stromal cells with genetic rescue of APC-trafficking defects by Ccl19 deletion.
limitations_preserved: Non-signaling scavenging/gradient-shaping edge rather than productive canonical GPCR relay; preserve inflammatory skin stromal context and distinguish CCL19 from CCL21.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC4901034, Atypical Chemokine Receptors and Their Roles in the Resolution of the Inflammatory Response; PMCID:PMC6176735, Chemokine Transport Dynamics in Lymphatic and Blood Vessels
primary_title: Scavenging of soluble and immobilized CCL21 by ACKR4 regulates peripheral dendritic cell emigration
decision_basis: The reviews identify ACKR4 as a CCL21 scavenger, and the cited primary study measures ACKR4 scavenging of soluble and immobilized CCL21 and links it to peripheral dendritic-cell emigration in mouse barrier tissues.
limitations_preserved: Scavenging is context- and ligand-form-dependent; preserve soluble versus immobilized/full-length or processed CCL21 boundaries and do not infer a canonical intracellular relay.
